sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Regensburg is cutting car access to its Altstadt and moving parking to the edge. Voters rejected continuing the Stadtbahn in a referendum on 9 June 2024, with 53.6% against on a turnout of 55.9% [10]. The council had decided in June 2018 to start planning two lines at an estimated €880 million [11]. Separately, the city is calming Altstadt traffic. A package approved by the planning committee on 15 July 2025, with SPD, Greens, Freie Wähler, ÖDP and BSW in favour and CSU and FDP against, lets cars enter the Altstadt only in set loops and removes public parking or converts it to resident parking. According to opposition speakers it leaves 123 fewer spaces [18]. The city says the plan runs to 2035, and its first phase began in October 2025 with bike lanes on Thundorferstraße, St.-Peters-Weg and Wöhrdstraße [20]. In May 2025 all public paid spaces in the Obermünsterviertel were replaced by 22 resident spaces, with the Petersweg garage and the Unterer Wöhrd lot named as alternatives [17].

The policy rests on older measures. A 2017 revision of the air quality plan named an Umweltzone as its main measure, covering the Altstadt inside the Alleengürtel [3], and Stadtwerk's 2023 media kit describes three inner-city garages as lying inside it [6]. Deutsche Umwelthilfe filed a court action in July 2019 over nitrogen dioxide [5]. A mobility survey from 2023 and 2024 found that, against 2018, walking and cycling had gained five points of the modal split and car use had lost four [16]. In July 2026 the city also extended morning delivery hours in the pedestrian zones by 30 minutes, at the request of retailers and hotels [24].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The main project is a new garage at the Unterer Wöhrd park-and-ride, which the council approved by 28 votes to 21 on 30 July 2025 [19]. The city had consulted in June 2024 on enlarging the area from about 670 to at most 1,400 spaces, citing parking lost in the Altstadt [9], and reported a budget of €18 million in September 2024 [14]. Construction began on 2 February 2026. During the works 138 spaces and all motorhome pitches are lost, leaving about 224 car spaces [21]. The groundbreaking described a garage of 580 spaces, about 1,000 including the open area, with 50 charge points and completion targeted for April 2027 [22]. The lot already became chargeable in July 2024, at €1 up to 12 hours and €2 for 12 to 24 hours, which the ACE motoring club criticised [12].

Stadtwerk Regensburg has also raised prices in its own garages. It abolished free parking time on 1 April 2022 [0][1], and from 1 April 2024 charged €0.60 per started half hour for the first hour, €1.10 per half hour up to 6.5 hours and €14 for 6.5 to 24 hours [2]. The TechCampus garage kept its prices [2]. That garage, with 377 spaces and 50 charge points, was built on a former barracks site [8]. A local group, the Freunde der Altstadt, said in July 2024 that Altstadt garage spaces had risen by 300 since 2014, a claim by an advocacy group [13]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Das Stadtwerk Regensburg runs four garages with almost 2,000 spaces: Petersweg (560), Dachauplatz (700), the Theater garage at Bismarckplatz (355) and TechCampus (377) [6]. The operators of the other garages in our data are not confirmed by any source we could open, and we have no price data for Regensburg. Our measured set is nine car parks with 4,774 spaces, two within 500 m of Neupfarrplatz (1,260 spaces) and five more within 1 km (2,672). The largest is the 1,548-space Regensburg Arcaden shopping-centre garage, 0.9 km from Neupfarrplatz.

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 53% on weekdays and 51% at weekends, a small gap. The fullest is the Unterer Wöhrd park-and-ride lot (87%), though it was losing capacity to building work during these weeks, which our 507-space figure may not reflect. Next come Dallmeier (68%), Theater/Bismarckplatz (67%), Petersweg (61%) and Dachauplatz (56%). The two garages within 500 m average 58%, against 44% for the five 500 m to 1 km out. The Arcaden, the largest, is only 34% full, and Arnulfsplatz is at 33%.

The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ, and we have no multi-year history for Regensburg.
